issues.legal_issue: The heirs of an allottee whose shop has been resumed may retain possession only on the terms of a case-specific order requiring full payment of the outstanding dues within the allowed time.
material_facts: The original allottee’s heirs remained in possession of the shop despite an order resuming it.
The purchase price and interest remained unpaid in full.
The heirs agreed to pay the amount specified by the authority by the deadline set by the Court.

The Court directed that timely payment would lead the authority to complete the allotment formalities; otherwise, the heirs had to surrender the shop, and the amount already paid would be treated as occupation charges.
issues.conclusion: The heirs could retain the shop if they paid the specified total, including miscellaneous charges, by 30 April 2015, in which event the authority was to complete the allotment formalities. If they did not pay by then, they had no right to retain possession, had to hand over the shop, and the authority could take possession; amounts paid so far would be treated as occupation charges. The Court stated that its order was not to be treated as a precedent because it was made on the peculiar facts of the case.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made a conditional, fact-specific order permitting retention upon timely full payment and requiring surrender upon nonpayment. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case and expressly stated that the order was not a precedent.

rule.if: appeal_from_resumption_order and heirs_remain_in_possession and purchase_dues_remain_unpaid and heirs_agree_to_pay

predicates.appeal_from_resumption_order: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an order that resumed an allotted property.
predicates.heirs_remain_in_possession: The allottee’s heirs continue to possess the property after the resumption order.
predicates.purchase_dues_remain_unpaid: The purchase price and related amounts remain unpaid in full.
predicates.heirs_agree_to_pay: The allottee’s heirs agree to pay the amount due.

issues.definition: When heirs remain in possession after an appealed resumption order, purchase dues remain unpaid, and the heirs agree to pay, retention is conditioned on timely full payment and nonpayment requires surrender.
